build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not picture 39: its packed bytes end on the disk where picture 40's packed bytes begin, and the unpacker reads on to the end of its 3-sector window, so these are those bytes decoded with picture 39's value table (side 3's, this snapshot's). Nothing reads them

comments.text: Picture 39's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$002F, channel 0's script at +$000E, channel 1's script at +$001B, channel 2's script at +$0025 and 0 for channel 3, which it does not use.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 4 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 5, frame 1 then 10, frame 1 then 6, frame 1 then 25. One pass takes 46 steps.

Channel 1's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 3 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 2 then 5, frame 3 then 10, frame 3 then 4. One pass takes 19 steps.

Channel 2's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 3 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 2 then 10, frame 4 then 8, frame 4 then 10. One pass takes 28 steps.

Picture 39's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $04 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 65 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 39, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1, 2, 3 and 4: a run count of 0 to start, then 10 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 68 bitmap bytes in all (1 run of a repeated byte among them), in columns 7 to 11. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 39, named by channel 1's entry 1 and channel 2's entry 1: empty, a run count of 0 and the $FF that ends the frame, so draw_frame_xor ($0648) changes nothing and the entry only waits.

Frame 3 of picture 39, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 2 and 3: a run count of 0 to start, then 5 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 109 bitmap bytes in all (8 runs of a repeated byte among them), in columns 1 to 3. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 4 of picture 39, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 2's entries 2 and 3: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 70 bitmap bytes in all (6 runs of a repeated byte among them), in columns 4 to 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Picture 39's own packed bytes go on past the last byte the picture code reads ($CCCA): 15 more bytes, decoded from the stream up to where picture 40's packed bytes begin on the disk. Nothing reads them; they read as ASCII "SITIONOMONPR#PR".
